subject: Re: Broadline MSA — tranche-based scope reallocation & fee smoothing
messages:
From: Broadline Procurement <procurement@broadline.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@broadline.com
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: reallocate MSA Exhibit into tranches + smoothing proposal

Markus —

Thanks for the kickoff last week. Broadline's execs reviewed the draft MSA and want to propose a tranche-based reallocation of Exhibit B (capacity) across Q3/Q4 to better match their projected usage. The ask is two-fold:

- Move 40% of the current Q3 throughput into a Q4 tranche (implementation still in Q3) so billing maps to expected consumption.
- Apply a fee-smoothing mechanism so the blended effective rate across the two tranches remains within 5% of the original schedule.

Attached is our annotated SOW (Broadline_SOW_redline_v1.docx) and a short fee-rebalance spreadsheet. Legal copied here (contracts@broadline.com) — they flagged a couple of MSA clauses they want clarified if we change Exhibit structure (notably the ramp/fallback and termination triggers).

Could you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Produce a single change order or multiple change orders (one per tranche) from your side;
2) Share an impact note on SLA and invoicing flow; and
3) Provide a recommended redline for the order form so Broadline's counsel has a clean version to review.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

— Jared Mills
Head of Procurement, Broadline Systems
procurement@broadline.com

Attachment: Broadline_SOW_redline_v1.docx (commented), fee-rebalance-spreadsheet.xlsx

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Broadline Procurement <procurement@broadline.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: reallocate MSA Exhibit into tranches + smoothing proposal

Jared —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redline. Quick answers up front:

1) We can issue either a consolidated change order that describes tranche allocations as Exhibit B-1/B-2, or separate change orders per tranche. For simplicity and fewer signature steps I usually recommend a single change order with annexed tranche tables.

2) SLA and invoice impact is minimal operationally — the serving runtime and capacity allocations are unchanged; billing will follow the amended Exhibit with prorated invoice lines. There are two edge cases to call out:
   - If Broadline exercises the fallback (early termination of a tranche), invoicing will require a true-up per existing MSA termination mechanics.
   - Burst/bandwidth credits tied to the original Q3 allocation need conscious re-mapping to the Q4 tranche to avoid over-provisioning.

3) I've asked legal to prepare a redline of our standard order form that references the new tranche annex. Irene (cc) will own the formal MSA clause language and the termination/ramp clarifications Broadline flagged.

Next steps I propose:
- Redwood to produce a draft consolidated change order + sample invoice lines (by EOD Thu).
- Internal review with legal and finance, then send clean redline to Broadline legal for their comments.
- Optional 30-min touchpoint tomorrow if you want to walk through the spreadsheet.

Looping in: Karthik for pricing confirmation, Laura for implementation sequencing, and Irene for legal redlines.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Office: +1 415-555-0172

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 15:26:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: reallocate MSA Exhibit into tranches + smoothing proposal

Markus / team —

Quick price/ops note after scanning the spreadsheet:

- We can meet the 5% blended-band target by offering a temporary Q3 credit equal to 30% of the per-token differential for the shifted capacity. That credit would apply on the first invoice post-change order and then amortize across Q4 invoices.
- Finance prefers a consolidated change order to avoid adding multiple invoice line templates per period — reduces ERP complexity.
- Implementation sequencing: Laura, can ops hold the additional Q4 allocations in a soft-reserved pool and mark them for Broadline starting 10/01? That avoids immediate capacity churn.

Irene — any immediate legal objections to combining tranches into one change order with an annex? My read: we need explicit language on ramp/fallback triggers, and a short carve-out describing how credits are applied.

Karthik
Director, Commercial Finance
redwood.ai

From: irene_choi@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Broadline Legal <contracts@broadline.com>, Broadline Procurement <procurement@broadline.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: reallocate MSA Exhibit into tranches + smoothing proposal

Jared / Broadline team —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. From legal's perspective we're comfortable with a consolidated Change Order that contains:

- Exhibit Annex A (Tranche Table) that maps the Q3/Q4 allocations, effective dates, and invoice codes.
- A short clause in the Order Form that:
  a) Clarifies when a tranche is considered "accepted" for billing (suggest: 7 days post-implementation validation window);
  b) Preserves the MSA termination/fallback mechanics and explicitly ties true-up calculations to the tranche-level executed quantities; and
  c) Documents the credit mechanism Karthik proposed (one-time credit applied to first invoice after Change Order; amortization schedule in annex).

I am attaching a preliminary redline of the Order Form and a tracked-change paragraph for the MSA ramp/termination section for your review. Please review and confirm:

- Broadline: are you comfortable with 7-day acceptance? If not, propose alternate.
- Markus/Karthik: confirm the credit language matches the finance workflow (one-time credit + amortization).

If we get agreement by EOD tomorrow, I'll prepare a clean change order for signature and a Docusign envelope with the consolidated Exhibit Annex.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
